personalInfo.name: Kaushal Kumar Agarwal
personalInfo.title: AI/ML Engineer | MCS @ Rice University
personalInfo.summary: Software Engineer with experience across backend, data/ML systems, and cloud platforms. Built scalable APIs, retrieval systems, and serverless data platforms. Strong in Python, Java, C#, AWS, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes, and modern web frameworks.

experience.description:
Leading RAG and agentic AI solutions end-to-end.

Timeline:
- Mid Feb – Early Apr: Researched knowledge-graph RAG using AWS Neptune and Neo4j AuraDB. Built pipelines to enrich JSON metadata for multi-format documents and construct graphs; prototyped natural-language → Cypher translation via LLM prompting/tool-calling to enable complex multi-hop queries.
- Apr – May: Built LLM-powered data cleaning to normalize hierarchical multi-tag columns in batches with guardrails and QC checks, reducing redundancy and improving downstream retrieval quality.
- May – Jul: Implemented a PDF chatbot that returns grounded answers with citations and page-level highlights. Built test/briefing document generation over multi-document sets using Amazon OpenSearch vector DB + Amazon Bedrock LLMs with re-ranking. In parallel, evaluated document/face detection (OpenCV, PaddleOCR, EasyOCR) to identify driver’s licenses and tuned extraction prompts.
- Late Jul – Aug: Productionized the chatbot and document generators with AWS Lambda and Step Functions; restricted actions strictly to one selected manual, added monitoring/alerts, and optimized latency/cost.

Agentic patterns: Tool-augmented LLMs orchestrating retrieval, re-ranking, citation extraction, page locator, OCR, and graph-query tools under policy constraints; evaluation harnesses and observability for reliability.
Managed grading and office hours for OOP, Computer Security, Software Engineering Methodology, and Software Construction; improved assignment scores by ~10% via targeted support.
Engineered C#/.NET backend APIs aggregating data from ~2,000 GitLab repos. Delivered role-based dashboards enabling leadership insights on MR review efficiency and developer performance.

Promoted to Software Engineer II within a year. Owned design and implementation of serverless APIs in Python on AWS Lambda to deliver new features and bug fixes. Managed Bitbucket CI/CD pipelines and Amorphic release cycles (dev → qa → staging → master), including packaging release artifacts to S3 and deploying via CMP. Provided on-call support for developers/customers, proactively shipped features, and patched production issues.

A) Dataset Metrics Collection (New Feature)
- Requirement: For each dataset (with many files, mutable over time), collect daily time series metrics (TotalFileSize, NumberOfFiles).
- Challenges: Full file scans are slow for Lambda; migrated to AWS Glue job, scheduled via CloudWatch Events (midnight), with backfill synchronization from dataset creation to present.
- Output: Time-series visualization to spot anomalies; automated email notifications to dataset owners.

B) Dataset Lifecycle Mechanism (Customer Demand)
- Requirement: Configure file expiration after X days and tier migration to specific S3 storage classes after Y days.
- Challenges: High-risk operation; used AWS Step Functions to orchestrate create/modify lifecycle rules at S3 prefix level with rollback on failures; robust error handling and notifications.
- Output: Increased customer trust and retention; contributed to revenue growth. Future: Glacier restore workflows.

C) AWS EKS Upgrade (1.21 → 1.24)
- Context: Cluster running Apache Superset and AWS Load Balancer Controller.
- Challenges: Reverse-engineered provisioning/install steps; extensive troubleshooting and compatibility validation.
- Result: Technically validated upgrade path; postponed due to limited customer engagement.

D) Error Code Standardization
- Goal: Unify exception message structure across services.
- Challenges: Designing a common error code template and consolidating multi-source error messages.
- Result: Improved code quality and operability.

E) Release Cycle Process
- Flow: dev → qa(testing) → staging(testing) → master(testing).
- Artifacts: Versioned release bundles in S3; used by CMP to deploy to customer environments.

F) Customer Environment Ops
- Patching Lambda processes; salt key rotation for PAT security.

G) Initiatives
- Piloted AWS CodeGuru (Code Reviewer, Lambda Profiler, Code Security).
- Reduced PyLint stage time by ~50% in Bitbucket pipelines.
- Researched observability (logs, traces, metrics) via AWS Grafana and CloudWatch Logs Insights.

Designed and developed a Scala-based Spark metrics framework to capture rich event data and accelerate performance analysis; achieved ~10% speedup on TPC-DS benchmarks. Optimized regression runs using PyTest with multiprocessing and Jenkins by parallelizing across ephemeral child accounts spawned from a parent account. Addressed per-account configuration reinitialization and teardown for isolation and reproducibility, reducing regression time roughly by a factor of N (number of cores).

J.A.R.V.I.S.S.: Contributed to a microservice-based multi-cloud security orchestration platform offering unified, cloud-agnostic terminology, tag-based policy enforcement resilient to cloud migrations, and cloud graph visualization to inspect live connections. Integrated AWS and GCP (extensible to Azure/Kubernetes/private clouds). Implemented components using Terraform, HashiCorp Vault, Flask, and MongoDB, leading to ~15% reduction in operational costs.

Developed decentralized applications using Flo-Blockchain: FloSecretSharingApp - Decentralized app to store secrets on blockchain using encryption with Shamir’s algorithm. FloAppStore - Python-based GUI app store (Tkinter), with all app metadata stored on blockchain. FloWhatsapp - Peer-to-peer web chat app using JavaScript, IndexedDB, Mongoose Client (C++), and blockchain.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Machine Learning – Associate
certifications.description: Earners of this badge have knowledge and skills in developing, deploying, maintaining, and monitoring ML solutions to meet AI/ML objectives. They know how to ingest, transform, validate, and prepare data for ML modeling. They have skills in implementing and operationalizing ML workloads in production. They can select modeling approaches and analyze model performance. They have the expertise to monitor ML solutions and to secure ML systems and resources.

certifications.name: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
certifications.description: Earners of this badge understand AI, ML, and generative AI concepts, methods, and strategies in general and on AWS. They can determine the correct types of AI/ML technologies to apply to specific use cases and know how to use AI, ML, and generative AI technologies responsibly. They are familiar with the AWS Global Infrastructure, core AWS services and use cases, AWS service pricing models, and the AWS shared responsibility model for security and compliance in the AWS Cloud.

certifications.name: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate
certifications.description: Earners of this certification have a comprehensive understanding on how to deploy, manage, and operate IT systems on the AWS Cloud. They demonstrated the ability to migrate on-premises workloads to AWS and monitor, scale, and secure systems on the AWS platform. Badge owners are able to provide guidance on implementing best practices for cloud operations.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
certifications.description: Earners of this certification have a comprehensive understanding of AWS services and technologies. They demonstrated the ability to build secure and robust solutions using architectural design principles based on customer requirements. Badge owners are able to strategically design well-architected distributed systems that are scalable, resilient, efficient, and fault-tolerant.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Developer – Associate
certifications.description: Earners of this certification have a comprehensive understanding of application life-cycle management. They demonstrated proficiency in writing applications with AWS service APIs, AWS CLI, and SDKs; using containers; and deploying with a CI/CD pipeline. Badge owners are able to develop, deploy, and debug cloud-based applications that follow AWS best practices.

certifications.name: EPFL – Big Data Analysis with Scala and Spark
certifications.description: Manipulating big data distributed over a cluster using functional concepts is rampant in industry, and is arguably one of the first widespread industrial uses of functional ideas. This is evidenced by the popularity of MapReduce and Hadoop, and most recently Apache Spark, a fast, in-memory distributed collections framework written in Scala. In this course, we'll see how the data parallel paradigm can be extended to the distributed case, using Spark throughout. We'll cover Spark's programming model in detail, being careful to understand how and when it differs from familiar programming models, like shared-memory parallel collections or sequential Scala collections. Through hands-on examples in Spark and Scala, we'll learn when important issues related to distribution like latency and network communication should be considered and how they can be addressed effectively for improved performance.

certifications.name: DeepLearning.AI – Neural Networks and Deep Learning
certifications.description: In the first course of the Deep Learning Specialization, you will study the foundational concept of neural networks and deep learning. By the end, you will be familiar with the significant technological trends driving the rise of deep learning; build, train, and apply fully connected deep neural networks; implement efficient (vectorized) neural networks; identify key parameters in a neural network’s architecture; and apply deep learning to your own applications. The Deep Learning Specialization is our foundational program that will help you understand the capabilities, challenges, and consequences of deep learning and prepare you to participate in the development of leading-edge AI technology. It provides a pathway for you to gain the knowledge and skills to apply machine learning to your work, level up your technical career, and take the definitive step in the world of AI.

certifications.name: University of Colorado – Hacking & Patching
certifications.description: In this MOOC, you will learn how to hack web apps with command injection vulnerabilities in a web site of your AWS Linux instance.   You will learn how to search valuable information on a typical Linux systems with LAMP services, and deposit and hide Trojans for future exploitation.  You will learn how to patch these web apps with input validation using regular expression. You will learn a security design pattern to avoid introducing injection vulnerabilities by input validation and replacing generic system calls with specific function calls.  You will learn how to hack web apps with SQL injection vulnerabilities and retrieve user profile information and passwords.  You will learn how to patch them with input validation and SQL parameter binding.  You will learn the hacking methodology, Nessus tool for scanning vulnerabilities, Kali Linux for penetration testing, and Metasploit Framework for gaining access to vulnerable Windows Systems, deploying keylogger, and perform Remote VNC server injection.  You will learn security in memory systems and virtual memory layout, and understand buffer overflow attacks and their defenses.  You will learn how to clone a Kali instance with AWS P2 GPU support and perform hashcat password cracking using dictionary attacks and known pattern mask attacks.
